PROSPECTUS 2026-27
Dr. Inderjeet Singh
Vice-Chancellor
It gives me immense pleasure to welcome you to Bihar Animal Sciences University
(BASU), one of the premier institutions in India for veterinary & animal husbandry, dairy, and
fisheries education. We are delighted that you are considering BASU for your higher education
journey.
At BASU, we strive to provide the best possible academic environment for our students to
excel in their respective fields. Our dynamic faculty and well-equipped laboratories are among the
many resources we provide to support your academic endeavours. Our faculty and staff are
committed to provide you with an exceptional education that will enable you to achieve your full
potential and become a successful professional in the livestock industry. We offer a wide range of
undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral programs, in different disciplines under veterinary
science, dairy science and technology and fisheries.
Our university has established linkages with various institutions, organizations, and
corporate houses to leverage the potential of both sides in our programs. Our graduates are serving
in India and abroad, in various capacities or excelling in their own exemplary enterprises, with
high stature and recognitions in the field of academics, research, and industry.
The academic reputation of BASU has always attracted meritorious candidates from all
over India. We hope that the new academic session 2026-27 will attract the best talent from all
parts of India, and the students will excel in academics, co-curricular, and extra-curricular
activities, so that they get transformed into proficient professionals to help the animal husbandry,
dairy, and fisheries sector in achieving the envisaged socio-economic national goals.
Once again, I extend my warm welcome to you to join us at BASU and become a part of
our thriving academic community.
Vice – Chancellor
Bihar Animal Sciences University,
Patna-800014
PROSPECTUS 2026-27
Dr. Pankaj Kumar Singh
Registrar (I/c)
Dear Students,
Warm Greetings,
The Veterinary Science & Animal Husbandry, Dairy and Fisheries indeed are highly noble
and rewarding profession. The field is diversifying and growing especially in livestock, fisheries
and poultry. These sectors have shown a rapid growth in past few decades and are contributing
significantly to the gross domestic product (GDP) of the country derived from agriculture. Good
health has become important not just for human being but also for animals. The Veterinary &
Animal Science, Dairy Technology and Fisheries sectors are the pillars contributing to the
technology led growth in achieving the nutritional security and wellbeing of mankind. In recent
years, emerging zoonotic diseases and food safety issues have been given priority at national and
international level.
The Veterinary, Dairy and Fisheries profession plays a very important role in, treatment,
diagnosis, production and conservation of livestock, fisheries and birds. There are many private
players taking up Veterinary & Animal Husbandry, Dairy and Fisheries as an entrepreneurship,
particularly in areas of modern farming, biotechnology, genetic engineering, nanotechnology,
vaccines, diagnostics, therapeutics, feed and value added animal and poultry products thereby
opening up new avenues for veterinary, dairy and fisheries graduates. Companion animals (dogs,
cats etc.) practice in cosmopolitan cities, establishment of dairy and poultry industries, milk and
meat processing centres, establishment of livestock business and marketing etc. are gaining
momentum. Even the demand for Veterinary, Dairy and Fisheries graduates for research, teaching
and extension in both, developed and developing countries is on a rise. Besides this, the
veterinarians also have opportunities for getting placements in the military, paramilitary,
municipal corporations, medical research, insurance, bank sector and State Animal Husbandry
Services. Veterinarians are also in great demand for the conservation and treatment of wild and
pet animals.
I am delighted to know that you are interested in pursuing your graduate studies with
specification in Veterinary Science & Animal Husbandry or Dairy or Fisheries. I am sure that at
the end of the academic career you will be all groomed to take up this profession to greater heights
with your zeal and enthusiasm.
I wish you a very bright and successful career.
Registrar
Bihar Animal Sciences University, Patna

Profile of the University
1.1 ABOUT THE UNIVERSITY
Bihar Animal Sciences University (BASU) has been established with its headquarters
at Patna through an act of Bihar State (BASU Act No. 15 of 2016, notified in the
Bihar Gazette on 29 August 2016). The University has two campuses and four
constituent Colleges viz. Bihar Veterinary College and Bihar State Institute of Dairy
Technology at Patna campus and College of Fisheries and College of Veterinary and
Animal Sciences at Kishanganj campus. Besides research facilities available in its
constituent colleges, the University also has research farms/research stations namely
Livestock Farm Complex, Patna; Poultry Research and Training Centre, Patna;
Government Buffalo Farm, Sipaya (Gopalganj) and Krishi Vigyan Kendra, Jamui.
The University headquarter is situated near Jai Prakash Narayan International Airport
at Patna.
1.2 OBJECTIVES
 To impart education in Veterinary Science, Animal Husbandry, Dairy, Poultry,
Fisheries and other allied branches of learning.
 To further the advancement of learning and conducting of research, particularly, in
Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Dairy, Fisheries and other allied sciences.
 To undertake the extension of education of such sciences and technologies that are
relevant for the livelihood of rural people of the state.
 To facilitate and ensure qualitative improvement in the teaching and learning
processes and methodology.
 To facilitate and ensure quality research in the contemporary and frontier areas of
animal science and technologies.
 To facilitate the need for an organized process of lifelong learning.
 To disseminate knowledge and findings emerging in the University, its colleges, and
institutions.
 To establish partnerships with the industries and other entities working in animal
science and technology and agriculture manufacturing.
 To establish Hospital for treatment/ research-role of the University.
 Such other purposes as the University or Government may advise from time to time.
 To establish Dairy processing plant for production of quality dairy products,
advancement of research and to import hands on training to the dairy students.

1.4 THE FACULTIES OF THE UNIVERSITY
1. Veterinary Science & Animal Husbandry
The faculty has two colleges i.e. Bihar Veterinary College (BVC), Patna and
College of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Kishanganj. The following
programs are offered at these colleges.
 Bachelor of Veterinary Science and Animal Husbandry (B.V.Sc.
& A.H.): It is a five years and six months’ degree program. It is
regularly offered at BVC, Patna and College of Veterinary and
Animal Sciences, Kishanganj.
 Master of Veterinary Science (M.V.Sc.) is offered in different
disciplines at BVC, Patna and COVAS, Kishanganj. It is a two-year
postgraduate program. Detailed information is given under section
2.13 and 3.17 respectively.
 Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) is offered at BVC, Patna in different
disciplines. It involves two semesters of course work and Four
semester thesis work to fulfil the degree requirements. Details of
disciplines and other information are given under section 2.14.
2. Dairy Technology
The faculty has one institution i.e. Bihar State Institute of Dairy Technology at
Patna, which offers the following academic programs:
 B. Tech. (Dairy Technology): It is a four years degree program and
regularly offered at BSIDT, Patna.

5.14.
 Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) is offered at Kishanganj in different
disciplines. It involves two semesters of course work and thesis work
to fulfil the degree requirements. Details of disciplines and other
information are given under section 5.15.

BIHAR VETERINARY COLLEGE, PATNA
2.1 INTRODUCTION
Bihar Veterinary College,
Patna, the 5th oldest Veterinary
College in pre-independence
India, was founded on 2nd April,
1927 by Sir Henry Wheeler, the
then Governor of Bihar & Orissa.
The College made remarkable
progress under the guidance and
supervision of Dr. R. T. Davis,
the first Principal of this historic
College with a team of renowned
scientists specialized in Breeding, Feeding, Management and Disease control of
Livestock and Poultry. During the post-independence period, Bihar Veterinary
College developed to its full capacity and occupied a prestigious status with strong
base for teaching and research in the field of Veterinary Science and Animal
Husbandry as well as advanced Veterinary clinical services to the society.
Bihar Veterinary College, Patna, for a long time, provided quality Veterinary
education and training not only to the candidates from Bihar and Orissa but also from
several other states (U.P., Meghalaya, Mizoram, Tripura, Jammu & Kashmir, Assam,
Himachal Pradesh etc.) of the country as well as from developing countries like
Nepal, Bhutan, Afghanistan, Iran, Malaysia etc. Graduates of this college are serving
across the world and have occupied coveted and prestigious positions in State and
Central Government, State Agricultural Universities, Research Institutes and National
as well as Multinational Industries. It can be mentioned with pride that Dr. C. M.
Singh, Dr. B. S. Rajya, Dr. R.C.P. Yadav, Dr. G. C. Mohanty, Dr. O. N. Singh, Prof.
A. Ahmad, Dr. H. R. Mishra, Dr. R. B. Prasad, Dr. V. S. Pandey, Dr. D. V. Singh, Dr.
G. Biswal, Dr. D. C. Nayak amongst others are the glittering graduates of this alma
mater.
2.2 FACILITIES AVAILABLE: Laboratories, Instructional Farm, Veterinary
Clinics, Hatchery etc.
All departments of the college are
well-equipped with modern
laboratories catering to undergraduate
teaching as per the norms of the
Veterinary Council of India (VCI) and
postgraduate teaching in accordance
with ICAR guidelines. The college
houses a dedicated centre/unit for the

comprehensive diagnosis of infectious and non-infectious animal diseases, serving as
a vital support system for both academic and field-level veterinary services.
The Veterinary Clinical Complex (VCC) is equipped with advanced diagnostic and
therapeutic facilities, including X-ray, endoscopy, ultrasonography, physiotherapy, a
specialized dental unit, blood biochemical analysis, histopathology, antibiotic
sensitivity testing, and molecular diagnostic techniques. Faculty members from the
Departments of Microbiology, Pathology, Parasitology, and Biochemistry work in
close coordination to provide integrated diagnostic services. Veterinary Pathology
plays a pivotal role in advancing animal health, safeguarding public health, and
promoting research by effectively bridging the gap between basic sciences and
clinical practice. A large number of clinical cases are routinely attended at the VCC,
where samples are processed with precision for accurate and timely diagnosis. In
addition to in-house cases, diagnostic samples are regularly received from field
veterinarians, government veterinary hospitals, farmers, and private practitioners.
Whenever necessary, faculty members from allied disciplines such as Pharmacology,
Animal Nutrition, Veterinary Public Health & Epidemiology, and Veterinary
Physiology extend their expertise in diagnostic and investigative procedures.
Confirmatory disease diagnosis remains a core strength of the institution, significantly
contributing to disease management and control strategies across the state.
Clinical and para-clinical departments are actively involved in the systematic
collection, preservation, transportation, and analysis of diverse biological samples.
These include morbid and necropsy materials, body fluids (such as discharges, blood,
serum, and plasma), tissues, urine, and faecal samples. Detailed microbiological,
pathological, parasitological, biochemical, and toxicological examinations are
conducted to ensure rapid and reliable diagnosis, thereby enabling veterinarians to

The college also actively participates in disease monitoring through both active and
passive surveillance under the All India Coordinated Research Projects (AICRP) on
Animal Disease Monitoring and Surveillance (ADMAS) and Foot & Mouth Disease
(FMD). These initiatives contribute to the generation of baseline epidemiological
data, which is crucial for evidence-based policy planning and disease control
programs in the state of Bihar.
To strengthen field-level clinical competence, Ambulatory Clinical Classes are
conducted for undergraduate students in two adopted villages twice a week (Monday
and Friday). This initiative provides hands-on exposure to real-time clinical cases
while simultaneously delivering veterinary healthcare services at the farmers’
doorstep.

2.5 STUDENT INTERNSHIP/EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING PROGRAMS
The Internship Programme is an integral component of the B.V.Sc. & A.H. degree
curriculum, undertaken by students for a period of twelve months after the successful
completion of the four-and-a-half-year academic coursework. Completion of all
prescribed theory and practical courses is mandatory for enrollment in the internship
programme. Students are divided into batches based on the total number of
candidates. During the internship, they undergo rotational training across various
clinical and para-clinical departments of the college, as well as at external institutions
such as Patna Zoo, Rajgir Zoo Safari, Government Veterinary Hospitals, poultry
farms, and other relevant field units. A significant portion of the internship—
particularly three months—is devoted to intensive clinical training in core areas such
as Veterinary Gynaecology & Obstetrics, Veterinary Medicine, and Veterinary
Surgery & Radiology. During this period, interns are entrusted with round-the-clock
clinical responsibilities, enabling them to develop practical skills in diagnosis,
treatment, emergency care, and case management. In addition, interns undergo hands-
on training in livestock production and management at the university’s Livestock
Farm Complex for a period of three weeks, where they gain exposure to modern
animal husbandry practices, breeding, feeding, and farm management techniques. As
per the norms of the Veterinary Council of India (VCI), students are also deputed to
reputed veterinary colleges and institutes in other states to broaden their exposure and
gain experience in diverse agro-climatic and management conditions. The programme
further includes interactions with experts and representatives from pharmaceutical and
animal health industries, which helps interns stay updated with recent advancements,
therapeutics, vaccines, and professional opportunities in the veterinary sector. Interns
are provided a monthly stipend of ₹15,000/- as per the Government of Bihar rules. At
the end of the internship programme, each student is evaluated based on their
performance, clinical competence, and overall conduct. Upon satisfactory completion,
the B.V.Sc. & A.H. degree is awarded, qualifying them to serve as competent
veterinary professionals in clinical practice, research, extension, and allied sectors.

2.10 EMPLOYABILITY
The students who are graduated from this college have 100% employability. Majority
of our graduates, around 80% are employed by the government sector in the
Department of Animal Husbandry as Veterinary Officers. Many of these veterinary
officers join after their B.V.Sc. & A.H. whereas around 15-20% joins after obtaining
their specialization. Around 5-10% of graduates who opt for higher studies find a
satisfying career in institutes of highest learning in research and academia
(universities, ICAR institutes) both in India and abroad. Veterinary graduate students
also join other reputed organizations like COMFED, JEEVIKA, RVC, SSB etc.
2.11 SPECIAL FACILITIES
VETERINARY EMERGENCY RESPONSE UNIT (VERU)
Veterinary Emergency Response Unit (VERU) was established in the college during
Kosi flood in the year 2008-09 in collaboration with World Animal Protection
(WAP), New Delhi. The basic objective of creating Veterinary Emergency Response
Unit in this college is to develop human resources capable of conducting rescue of
animals during disaster and also to prevent any outbreak of diseases post disaster as
well as to conduct impact of such incidents and be prepared for future. The training
comprises of a series of lectures spread over 4- days rigorous training including and
field exercises.
Under this program the students were exposed to five days’ theory classes on
prefix animal disaster lecture module and one-day simulation exercise at 9th Battalion
NDRF, Bihta (Bihar) and got hands-on- training. This program is first of its kind in
the country which imparts specialized training to Veterinary students.
Regular training of veterinary doctors of the Animal Husbandry department,
GOB is being imparted apart from training to NDRF and SSB personnel. Training has
also been organized for trainers by VERU unit of this college. This helps in creating
human resources capable of working as trainers and work under disaster situations to
save precious livestock.
